rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: wide one-paragraph prompt. Four paragraphs by move: board read; file read; task; save. Closest: paragraph 3 holds four sentences (prompt L5) but each is a full-stopped move that reads the same aloud; condensed-in-fence carve-out applies.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Orient saved rule by where it FIRES, not surface activity producing it.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: not a save-the-rule prompt

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: lead-in and fence read as two drafts. L29 'Ask Claude to read the board and add what the three of you did not see' vs prompt opening 'Read the pre-mortem frame on our team's Miro board' ... 'Add the causes we missed': same verbs (read, add) and noun (the board). Rhymes.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Declare `permission-mode:` when paste requires specific Claude Code mode.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: permission mode not load-bearing; none declared

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify session boundary before deciding prompt's context-carrying.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: warm-session referent absent. Prompt carries its own context: names the board frame, reads team/chosen-bet.md and team/<name>/ from disk, no 'the thing we just did'. Closest definite reference: 'the frame' (prompt L5) is introduced by the first sentence. Works cold or warm.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact-vs-STOP tail ordering — last imperative wins.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: STOP after write blocks the artifact. Last imperative is the artifact: prompt L7 'Then save every sticky to team/premortem.md'. No STOP/ask-and-wait tail.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headless-runner discipline — tail every prompt with no-AUQ guard.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: student-interactive, not a headless-runner prompt

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Long-running prompts stream progress — never go silent.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: not a long-running prompt; reads one board frame

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A leading-looking line can be a forcing function; prefer the simpler prompt.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: tidying a load-bearing leading line. 'Lean toward what we seem to assume will go fine' (prompt L5) is the forcing function against restating board stickies; kept, nothing added. Prompt stays plain 'do X'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompt paths match Builder scope.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: Agents 101 scoping rule; APT101 paths are team/ relative

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Output shape — trust Claude's defaults, don't pad.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: padded output shape. Shape specs are the teaching content only: 'past tense, with the early warning sign we would have seen in week two', 'at most three'. No trailing title/format spec.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: "Add X and regenerate" is a trap.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no add-and-regenerate

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Vary closings deliberately.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: closing mechanic is a pedagogy choice, not a prompt-mechanics call

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A take-home prompt asks for one bounded build.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: not a take-home prompt

platform_claims_checked.claim: Ask Claude to read the board and add what the three of you did not see (Claude reads and writes stickies on the Miro frame via the connector)
Sticky and dot colours tell you whose they are (a read carries colour and position, not author)

notes: Both platform claims are backed by the repo's own live-test notes (curriculum/module-design/miro.md, tested 2026-10-07; read frames, write stickies into a frame, dots read back with fill+position, no author on a sticky), hence 'inferred' is the closest enum value; they are not from the compendium or claude-code-guide. Pedagogy rows limited to technical sub-rules 16,22,23,36,37 (template scope); the brief carried all 69. Rule question for maintainer, not filed: check_prompts 1 vs the path pattern 'team/<name>/' in prompt L3; harm (unfilled placeholder) is absent because Claude lists team/ subfolders.
